chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Khathʿamī, from Muḥammad ibn Buhlūl al-ʿAbdī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: “Allah does not secure the believer from the turmoils of the world, but He secures him from blindness in it and from misery in the Hereafter.”

key_terms.الْآخِرَةِ: the Hereafter, the final life after death
key_terms.الْعَمَى: blindness; here, spiritual blindness and misguidance
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer; the one characterized by iman

ai.seo_question: Does Allah protect the believer from worldly trials or from spiritual loss and punishment in the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the mu'min is not necessarily spared worldly upheavals and trials. Rather, Allah grants the believer a greater protection: safety from inner blindness in this world and from wretchedness in the Hereafter. Its significance lies in redirecting the measure of divine care from worldly ease to guidance and ultimate salvation.
